case_title: Pradeep Kumar v. State of Chhattisgarh
confession: Extra judicial confession of the accused, which was not supported by other evidence and was hit by s.27 of the Evidence Act
aggravating_circumstances: Prior animosity between the accused and the deceased
mitigating_circumstances: No independent corroborated material except for the confessional statement of the accused, which also is not proven on record
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Rs.500/-
high_court_outcome: Upheld the conviction of the appellant and acquitted co-accused
neutral_facts: The prosecution case rested on three circumstances: the alleged confessional statement of the accused, prior animosity between the accused and the deceased, and the recovery of materials from the accused. The trial court convicted both accused based on these circumstances, relying on the confessional statement and the recovery of items. The high court upheld the conviction of the appellant but acquitted the co-accused. The supreme court found that the confessional statement was not supported by other evidence and that the recovery of materials lacked independent corroboration. The court also found the testimonies of key witnesses unreliable and the investigation incomplete, leading to the acquittal of the appellant.
